Uses exactly your own settings.
Each game connection gets its own lane, so one busy stream can\'t hold up your game packets.
Domain routing keeps working without rewriting the game server\'s address.
No extra DNS lookup before routing, saving a round trip on each new connection.
Smaller packets avoid fragmentation on mobile networks, so fewer packets get lost.
Games, calls and video use UDP; it stays allowed.
Lookups are encrypted (DNS-over-HTTPS) and go through the tunnel, so your ISP can\'t see the sites you open.
IPv6 is dropped inside the tunnel instead of risking a leak around it.
Apps fall back to TCP/TLS through the tunnel, which is harder to fingerprint.
Your handshake looks like Chrome\'s, so it blends in with normal browsing.
Routes by the real site name, so rules match correctly.
Everything, including domestic sites, goes through the tunnel: nothing leaves outside it.
Large video streams don\'t share one connection, so they don\'t slow each other.
Full-size packets give the best throughput for video.
Lets streaming domains be routed correctly.
Many requests share a few connections, so the radio wakes up less often.
Ad domains are blocked (when your rules file includes them), saving data and battery.
Fewer parallel UDP flows keeps background traffic down.
Exactly your settings, no surprises
